title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Maya Rodriguez
content:
Summary

This page consolidates Redwood's employee-facing handbook material: what it's like to work here, role families and career ladders, core benefits and perks, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and the internal tools new hires will use. It is intended for all Redwood employees and hiring managers.

1) Working at Redwood — mission, values, and ways of working

Introduction:
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for production-grade LLM inference. We prioritize reliability, measurable product metrics, and a culture of engineering excellence. Our ways of working emphasize asynchronous collaboration, documented decisions, and user-centered product thinking.

Core principles (short):
- Prioritize customer reliability and cost-efficiency in product decisions.
- Ship small, iterate quickly, and measure impact.
- Document decisions (ADRs) and surface tradeoffs.
- Respect timezones and prefer async design reviews with optional syncs for alignment.

Working norms and expectations:
- Core hours: 10:00–16:00 local PT overlap for cross-functional teams; flexible schedules otherwise.
- Meeting etiquette: add an agenda, timebox to 45 minutes maximum by default, and capture decisions/action items in the meeting notes.
- Code review SLO: maintainers should respond to PRs within 48 hours on working days.

2) Roles & career ladders

Overview:
Redwood organizes career ladders by functional families: Engineering (BE/FE/Infra/SRE/Runtime), Applied ML, Product, Design, Developer Experience, Data, Security, People Ops, Finance, and Sales/Customer Success. Each family has leveled expectations (IC1–IC6 / Manager 1–3).

Career ladder summary table (high level):
| Family | Typical titles | IC levels | Manager levels | Core competencies |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Engineering | Software Engineer, Senior, Staff, Principal | IC2–IC6 | Mgr1–Mgr3 | Systems design, reliability, performance, mentorship |
| Applied ML | ML Engineer, Research Engineer | IC2–IC6 | Mgr1–Mgr3 | Model evaluation, data curation, on-device inference |
| Product | PM, Sr PM, Principal PM | IC2–IC5 | Mgr1–Mgr2 | Product strategy, roadmaps, cross-functional influence |

Promotion & leveling process (abridged):
1. Candidate prepares a self-review using the role family rubric and evidence (projects, metrics, architecture docs, feedback).
2. Manager performs a draft assessment and recommends level and comp.
3. Calibration panel (peer managers and a People Ops representative) reviews evidence and provides decision within the next cycle (typically 4 weeks).
4. Outcome communicated with development plan and follow-up goals if not promoted.

Expectations by level (examples):
- IC2: Owns features end-to-end, writes clear tests and docs, participates in on-call rotations.
- IC4 (Staff): Leads cross-team initiatives, mentors multiple engineers, influences architecture.
- Manager 1: Delivers team commitments, hires and grows direct reports, handles performance conversations.

3) Benefits & perks

Core benefits (standard US offering — summary):
- Health: PPO and HMO options, dental, and vision. Employer pays 80%+ of employee premium; family plans available.
- Financial: 401(k) with employer match (4% up to company policy), competitive RSUs and equity grants at hire and on level changes.
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO (accrual), 12 weeks parental leave (primary), 6 weeks for secondary caregivers, plus company holidays (10 days) and floating holidays.
- Wellbeing: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), mental health counselling, and monthly wellbeing stipend ($50).
- Professional development: $2,000 annual learning stipend, internal mentoring program, and conference budget approval process.
- Remote/office: Flexible remote-first policy with optional office hubs; travel reimbursement for onboarding week and team offsites.

Perks and allowances:
- Home office stipend ($300 one-time), second-monitor program, and noise-cancelling headset reimbursement.
- Commuter benefits where available and fitness reimbursement in select regions.

How to access benefits (process):
1. New hires receive benefits packet on Day 1 via HR portal (Greenhouse/Workday links depending on region).
2. Enrollment window: first 30 days. For questions, contact benefits@redwood.com or your People Ops partner.

4) Hiring and onboarding overview

Hiring principles:
- Hire for impact and learning ability. We value clear communication, systems thinking, and pragmatic engineering.
- Diverse interview panels with standardized rubrics to reduce bias.
- Offer approval requires People Ops, hiring manager, and a compensation review.

Interview stages (typical for engineering):
1. Recruiter screen (30m) — role fit and logistics.
2. Technical screen (45–60m) — coding or systems design.
3. Onsite / virtual loop (4–5 interviews) — design, coding, collaboration, and culture fit.
4. Debrief & decision — hiring manager + interviewers + People Ops.

Offer & negotiation:
- Standard offer includes base salary, equity grant, and benefits summary. Counter-offers handled by People Ops to maintain internal equity.

Onboarding plan (30/60/90):
- Pre-boarding (before Day 0): equipment shipped, account access requests raised (IT ticket), and first-week calendar scheduled by hiring manager.
- Day 1: Welcome orientation, HR benefits walkthrough, security & code of conduct, and manager 1:1 to set expectations.
- Week 1: Team introductions, systems access (see internal tools list), and first small-ticket project assigned.
- 30-day goals: deliver a scoped change end-to-end, complete required trainings, and present a short "what I learned" demo to the team.
- 60-day goals: own a medium-sized project and contribute to a roadmap discussion.
- 90-day goals: demonstrate steady velocity, document systems you rely on, and propose at least one improvement.

New hire checklist (to be completed by manager and new hire):
- Accounts: Slack, Google Workspace, Redwood Console (internal), GitHub, Jira, CI/CD build access.
- Security: Complete SSO onboarding, 2FA setup, and data handling training.
- Hardware: Confirm receipt of laptop, monitor, and peripherals.
- Mentorship: Assign a peer buddy and schedule weekly syncs for first 30 days.

5) Internal tools & guides

Core internal tools (how to access and owners):
- Slack (real-time comms): join #team-<team> channels; owners: eng-platform.
- Google Workspace (docs, calendar): People Ops provides initial access.
- GitHub (code): request org access via IT ticket; link to README and CODEOWNERS.
- Jira (work tracking): project-specific boards; product managers own templates and workflows.
- Redwood Console (internal ops/observability): request role-based access; eng-platform and SRE are owners.
- CI/CD (Buildkite or GitHub Actions): access requested via infra team; follow repo CONTRIBUTING.md for pipeline etiquette.
- Security & secrets (Vault/KMS): access approved by eng-security with least-privilege principle.

Access request process (step-by-step):
1. New hire manager opens an IT onboarding ticket with required access list within 3 business days of signing.
2. IT & security approve and provision accounts within 48–72 hours. If escalation is required, contact it-support@redwood.com with the ticket ID.

Tooling best practices and training:
- Every repo must include CONTRIBUTING.md and a short local dev setup doc.
- Use feature branches for work; open PRs early and request at least one reviewer.
- Run local integration tests before pushing changes that touch infra or model-serving code.
- New hires should complete the internal "Platform Fundamentals" self-paced course within 14 days.

6) Performance reviews & compensation cycles

Cadence and expectations:
- Formal performance reviews: semi-annual review cycles (mid-year and year-end). Managers gather peer feedback and measure against the career ladder rubric.
- Salary review: annual compensation review following the end-of-year performance cycle. Promotions can happen outside cycle for exceptional cases.

Review process (summary):
1. Self-review submitted 2 weeks before manager calibration.
2. Manager writes evaluation and calibration panel convenes.
3. Outcomes communicated with written feedback and next-step goals.

7) People Ops contacts and escalation

Primary contacts:
- People Ops general: people-ops@redwood.com
- Benefits & payroll: benefits@redwood.com
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.com
- IT & equipment: it-support@redwood.com

Escalation flow:
- For unresolved benefits or payroll issues: escalate to People Ops lead (Leah Kim) after 5 business days.
- For urgent security or incident-related access: contact eng-security@redwood.com and follow the incident runbook.

8) FAQ & quick links

FAQ (short):
- "Who do I talk to about parental leave?" — benefits@redwood.com.
- "How do I request additional hardware?" — open an IT ticket with justification.
- "Where are PR policies documented?" — See repo-level CONTRIBUTING.md and eng-developer-experience docs.

Quick links (internal):
- Onboarding checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/onboarding-checklist-2026
- Career ladder rubrics: /confluence/company-handbook/career-ladders-2026
- Benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.internal

Ownership and maintenance:
- Owned by People Ops; maintained quarterly or when policy changes. For content edits or corrections, submit a pull request to the handbook repo or email people-ops@redwood.com.
